fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the road.
• Clear any vegetation that narrows or overhangs the driveway to maintain a full-width, unobstructed driving path to the residence.
• Trim shrubs and low-hanging branches along walkways connecting the main residence to the detached structure so responders can move quickly between buildings.
• Post the street address visibly at the front entry area so it is readable from the street at night.
• Keep a clear path between the vehicle parking area and the front entry so parked vehicles do not block responder movement to the door.
• Mark or identify any secondary access points on the property so responders arriving from different directions can locate them quickly.
• Keep gates or passages between the main residence and detached structure unlocked or fitted with a consistent lock to allow responder access without delay.
• Thin dense vegetation around the detached structure so responders can approach and work around all sides of the building.
• Identify and mark a flat, firm staging area near the parking zone where emergency vehicles and equipment can be set up without blocking access routes.
• Confirm the detached structure has visible address or unit marking so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the clusters closest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure to reduce the path fire could take from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Trim shrubs and plants growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Separate the scattered trees from nearby vegetation clusters by removing the plants and brush growing between them.
• Clear dead leaves, branches, and plant debris from the ground beneath tree clusters near the structure.
• Keep branches trimmed back from rooflines, eaves, and any openings in the structure.
• Remove any dry or dead plant material from the bases of large trees closest to the building.
• Maintain the open terrain areas by keeping them free of encroaching shrubs or woody plant growth.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and overgrown vegetation along their edges.
• Maintain the existing open separation between vegetation and the structure by preventing new plant growth from closing that gap.
